name_en: Kankoro mochi — sun-dried sweet potato slices pounded together with glutinous rice
summary_ja: 薄くスライスして天日干ししたさつまいも「かんころ」を、もち米と合わせてつきあげた餅。高価なもち米を節約しながら家族全員が食べられる冬の保存食として、五島地方の各家庭でつくられてきたという。
summary_en: Sweet potato is sliced thin, sun-dried into "kankoro," and pounded together with glutinous rice into a mochi — said to have been made at home across the Goto islands as a winter keeping food that stretched costly rice to feed the whole family.
source_title: かんころ餅 長崎県

name_en: Ojika peanut tofu — ground peanuts bound with kudzu starch into a firm, chilled block
summary_ja: 島の特産である落花生をすり潰し、葛粉と合わせて練り固めた小値賀島の郷土食。ご飯のおかずには柚子味噌を添え、黒蜜やきなこ砂糖をかければスイーツにもなるという、赤土と潮風が育てた落花生を生かす一品。
summary_en: Peanuts grown on the island are ground and bound with kudzu starch into a firm block — a specialty of Ojika Island said to make a savory side with yuzu miso or a sweet with black syrup and sugared soybean flour, built on peanuts raised in red soil and sea wind.
source_title: ピーナッツ豆腐 長崎県

name_en: Nagasaki milk seiki — a spoon-eaten frozen dessert of milk, egg, and crushed ice
summary_ja: 牛乳と卵、砂糖、砕いた氷を合わせてつくる、スプーンで食べるシャーベット状の冷菓。大正末期から昭和初期、長崎市の喫茶店『ツル茶ん』が夏の暑さをしのぐためにつくったのが始まりとされる。
summary_en: Milk, egg, sugar, and crushed ice are blended into a sherbet-like frozen dessert eaten with a spoon — said to have begun in the late Taisho or early Showa era at Nagasaki's Tsuruchan cafe, devised to help customers through the summer heat.
source_title: 長崎ミルクセーキ 長崎県

name_en: Kanzarashi — small rice-flour dumplings chilled in spring water and drizzled with sweet syrup
summary_ja: 白玉粉でつくった小さな団子を島原の湧水で冷やし、砂糖やはちみつの蜜をかけて食べる冷たい菓子。1792年の島原大変で湧き出た地下水を生かした知恵とされ、かつては夏のもてなし用の菓子だったという。
summary_en: Small dumplings made from rice flour are chilled in Shimabara's spring water and drizzled with a sugar or honey syrup — said to make use of groundwater that began welling up after the 1792 Shimabara disaster, once a summer sweet reserved for entertaining guests.
source_title: かんざらし 長崎県
